aspect: The scale, with the spread between sources stated
description: UNICEF states one in every five of the world's out-of-school children is in Nigeria. Figures range from about 10.5 million aged 5-14 to estimates of 18.3 million, depending on year and age range.
energy_note: One in five of all the out-of-school children on earth.

description: A UNICEF official put it at 60% of 18.5 million being girls, with roughly a 20% difference between male and female enrolment and retention. In the north-east and north-west, female primary net attendance is 47.7% and 47.3% - meaning more than half the girls are not attending.
energy_note: More than half the girls in the north, not in school.

description: Millions of boys are sent far from home to study under traditional Qur'anic teachers and often forced to beg for survival. The system has existed for over 800 years. In 2010 the Universal Basic Education Commission estimated 9.5 million Almajiri nationwide.
energy_note: Nine and a half million children, studying and begging.

description: Sokoto recorded 249,523 Almajiri and out-of-school adolescent girls; Katsina 148,252 (86,757 boys, 61,495 girls); Jigawa 110,580 (56,159 boys, 54,421 girls).
energy_note: A quarter of a million, in one state.

description: Attacks on schools and abduction of students deter parents over safety concerns. In the north-east 2.8 million children need education-in-emergencies support and at least 802 schools remain closed.
energy_note: Eight hundred schools shut, and the children counted as truant.

aspect: The cost lands thirty years later
description: Out-of-school at eight produces the literacy gap at eighteen, the informal employment at twenty-five in WRK-001, and the inability to contest the inheritance in WOM-004 at fifty.
energy_note: A decision made about a six-year-old, priced at a lifetime.
